name: Chennai authoritative geometry source audit
scope: Chennai District and Greater Chennai Corporation, with OMR overlaps retained as unresolved revenue-to-municipal crosswalk work.

decision.summary: Official municipal geometry is discoverable and technically queryable, but MITO has not received permission to reproduce it. No boundary or road geometry has been copied, stored, plotted or redistributed.
decision.nextAction: Obtain written reuse permission from Greater Chennai Corporation and TNeGA/TNGIS, then capture a versioned source snapshot and reconcile ward, revenue-village and registration identifiers before plotting.

sources.title: EDPMobile2025 ArcGIS Feature Service
sources.rightsEvidence: GCC's copyright policy says portal material may be reproduced only after proper permission from the respective organization or department, with accurate reproduction and prominent source acknowledgement.
qualityNotes: The service publishes stable layer IDs, municipal ward and zone fields, geometry types and a declared projected coordinate system.
The service metadata has no populated copyright text or layer description; MITO therefore applies GCC's portal-wide copyright policy.
A municipal ward or road feature does not by itself establish a revenue-village, registration-village, street guideline record or parcel boundary.

sources.authority: Tamil Nadu Geographical Information System, TNeGA
sources.title: CUMTA Map Editor and TNGIS administrative layers
sources.rightsEvidence: TNGIS terms restrict publishing or sharing portal GIS data without prior approval and require approval for commercial applications; ownership remains with the contributing departments.
qualityNotes: The public interface proves that relevant administrative layers exist, but MITO has not verified a redistributable geometry endpoint, feature identifier contract or coordinate system for the revenue-village layer.
The layer is not used to infer a registration crosswalk or parcel boundary.

sources.title: Map of Chennai District
sources.rightsEvidence: The district website's copyright policy allows reproduction only after permission is obtained and the source is prominently acknowledged.
qualityNotes: The map is suitable as an official visual reference, not as a machine-readable revenue-village or parcel geometry source.
MITO will not digitize or trace the map into claimed exact boundaries without source geometry and an approved reuse method.

requirements: Written permission that covers storage, transformation, map display and redistribution for MITO's intended use.
A dated source snapshot with checksums, layer metadata, coordinate system and record counts.
Deterministic reconciliation between municipal ward or road IDs, revenue villages and registration villages.
Geometry validation for bounds, validity, duplicates and positional evidence before any plotted status is promoted.
